answer: Marble Routing Depth. Each agent’s reachability is weighted by the diversity of disjoint paths through which peers can route requests; a cluster whose members only reach the network through each other collapses to a shallow local marble. Peers allocate work proportionally to that depth, so a sybil farm must sustain many independently routed connections, each incurring real bandwidth and latency costs. A single pearl of genuine traffic cannot mask the missing walnut of diverse routes the attacker must pay to build.
